story.iWant: to analyze my win rates across different roles and game scenarios
story.soThat: I understand my strengths and weaknesses in various situations

tasks.task:
Create API endpoint for win rate analysis
Create `GET /api/players/[id]/analytics/win-rates` route handler Implement query parameters support: `dateRange?`, `roles?` (array of roles) Add authentication middleware (verify user owns player ID or is admin) Implement win rate calculation logic (overall, per-role, by scenario if available) Calculate comparison to average win rates (if aggregated data available) Add input validation using Zod schemas Return `WinRateAnalysis` response matching tech spec data model Add error handling (404 for player not found, 400 for invalid parameters) Add unit tests for API endpoint

Create domain service for win rate calculation
Create `WinRateAnalyzer` service in `src/domain/services/` Implement overall win rate calculation: (wins / total_games) × 100 Implement per-role win rate calculation: (wins in role / games in role) × 100 Implement scenario-based win rate calculation (tournament vs casual, if data available) Implement comparison to average win rates (if aggregated data available) Handle edge cases (no games, insufficient data, division by zero) Add unit tests for calculation logic

Create database query for win rate data
Create Prisma query to fetch game participation data with win/loss records Filter by player ID, date range, and roles Aggregate wins and losses by role Aggregate wins and losses by scenario (tournament vs casual) if tournament data available Add database indexes if needed (player_id, role, game_date, tournament_id) Optimize query performance (target < 500ms for aggregated data) Add integration tests for database queries

Create WinRateAnalysis component
Create `WinRateAnalysis` component in `src/components/analytics/` Use TanStack Query to fetch data from API endpoint Display overall win rate percentage prominently (large number, card component) Display per-role win rate breakdown (cards or table) Display bar chart comparing win rates across roles (Recharts BarChart) Display pie chart showing win/loss distribution (Recharts PieChart) Display scenario-based win rates (if available) with conditional rendering Display comparison to average win rates (if available) with visual indicators Connect to analytics store (Zustand) for filter state (date range, roles) Implement loading states (skeleton screens) Implement empty states for no data Add smooth animations for data loading/updates Make charts responsive (mobile: stacked, desktop: side-by-side) Add component tests using React Testing Library

Create win rate chart components
Create `WinRateBarChart` component for role comparison Create `WinLossPieChart` component for win/loss distribution Use Recharts library with lazy loading for code splitting Add hover tooltips showing exact percentages and counts Add color coding (green for wins, red for losses, role-specific colors) Make charts responsive with ResponsiveContainer Add smooth animations (300ms transitions) Add component tests

Integrate win rate analysis into analytics dashboard
Add `WinRateAnalysis` component to analytics dashboard page Connect to filter state (Zustand store) for date range and roles Implement filter application triggering data refetch Add smooth transitions when filters change (< 300ms) Test filter integration

Add TypeScript types and interfaces
Define `WinRateAnalysis` interface matching tech spec data model Define `WinRateAnalysisProps` interface Define `WinRateAnalysisResponse` interface for API response Add types for API request/response Ensure type safety throughout component tree Add JSDoc comments for all public interfaces

Add error handling and edge cases
Handle API errors (network, 404, 400) with user-friendly messages Display empty states for no win rate data Handle loading states gracefully Handle missing scenario data gracefully (conditional rendering) Handle missing aggregated data gracefully (show win rates without comparison) Add retry logic for failed API calls (exponential backoff, 3 attempts) Add error boundary for component errors Handle edge cases (no games, division by zero, single role data)

Performance optimization
Implement TanStack Query caching (5-minute stale time, 10-minute GC time) Add database query optimization (indexes, efficient aggregations) Lazy load chart libraries (code splitting) Optimize component re-renders (React.memo if needed) Optimize chart rendering for large datasets Measure and verify performance targets (< 500ms API response, < 2s chart render)

Testing
Unit tests for `WinRateAnalyzer` service (80%+ coverage) Integration tests for API endpoint (various query parameters, error cases) Component tests for `WinRateAnalysis` (rendering, loading states, empty states, charts) Component tests for chart components (bar chart, pie chart) E2E test: Complete flow (load dashboard → view win rates → apply filters → verify charts update)

criterion.given: I have game data with win/loss records per role

then.assertion: the system displays overall win rate percentage (prominent display)
win rate breakdown by role (Don: X%, Mafia: Y%, Sheriff: Z%, Citizen: W%)
win rate by scenario (tournament games vs casual games, if available)
comparison to average win rates (if aggregated data available)
visual charts: bar chart comparing win rates across roles, pie chart showing win/loss distribution

criterion.given: I have game data with win/loss records per role
criterion.when: I view the win rate breakdown

then.assertion: the system calculates and displays overall win rate: (total wins / total games) × 100
per-role win rates: (wins in role / games in role) × 100 for each role (Don, Mafia, Sheriff, Citizen)
win/loss counts for each role (wins, losses, total games)
win rate comparison chart showing relative performance across roles

criterion.given: I am viewing win rate analytics
criterion.when: I apply date range or role filters

then.assertion: the system updates all win rate calculations and charts to reflect the filtered data
the charts smoothly animate to the new data
the filter indicators show active filters

criterion.given: I have tournament and casual game data (if available)

then.assertion: the system displays win rate by scenario: tournament games win rate (if tournament data available), casual games win rate (if casual data available), comparison between tournament and casual performance
if scenario data is not available, the system gracefully handles the absence without errors

criterion.given: aggregated player data is available (if implemented)

then.assertion: the system displays comparison to average win rates: player's overall win rate vs average overall win rate, player's per-role win rates vs average per-role win rates, visual indicators showing above/below average performance
if aggregated data is not available, the system displays win rates without comparison

criterion.given: I am viewing win rate analytics

then.assertion: the system displays loading states (skeleton screens or spinners)
when data is available, it transitions smoothly with animations

criterion.given: I have no game data or insufficient data for win rate calculation

then.assertion: the system displays an empty state with helpful messaging

doc.section: AC3: Win Rate Analysis Across Roles
doc.snippet: Win Rate Analysis enables players to analyze win rates across different roles and game scenarios. The system displays overall win rate percentage, win rate breakdown by role (Don, Mafia, Sheriff, Citizen), win rate by scenario (tournament vs casual if available), comparison to average win rates (if aggregated data available), and visual charts (bar chart comparing win rates, pie chart showing win/loss distribution).

constraint.rule: Follow Clean Architecture + Hexagonal Architecture patterns. Analytics components in Presentation Layer (src/components/analytics/), domain services in Domain Layer (src/domain/services/), repositories in Infrastructure Layer (src/infrastructure/persistence/), API routes in Adapters Layer (src/app/api/).

Use TanStack Query for server state (analytics data) with 5-minute stale time and 10-minute GC time. Use Zustand store (src/store/analyticsStore.ts) for client state (filters). Connect WinRateAnalysis component to analyticsStore for date range and role filters.

Use ShadCN/UI base components with custom styling. Use Tailwind CSS 3.3.0 with tailwind-variants for component variants. Follow established component patterns from ELOTrendsChart and RoleMetricsDisplay.

Use Recharts library (^3.6.0) for bar charts and pie charts. Lazy load chart components via React.lazy with Suspense for code splitting. Use ResponsiveContainer with 300ms debounce for mobile performance. Animation settings: animationEasing="ease-in-out", animationDuration={300}.

Follow established request/response format patterns in src/app/api/players/[id]/analytics/. Use Next.js App Router API routes. Add authentication via authenticateRequest() middleware. Verify user owns player ID or is admin. Use Zod schemas for input validation. Return proper error codes (404 for not found, 400 for invalid parameters, 401 for auth errors, 500 for server errors).

TypeScript 5.0.0 with strict mode. Maintain type safety throughout component tree. Define all interfaces in src/types/analytics.ts. Add JSDoc comments for all public interfaces. Use type inference where appropriate but be explicit for API contracts.

API response time target: < 500ms for aggregated data. Chart rendering target: < 2 seconds for initial render. Filter application target: < 300ms for data refresh. Implement database indexes on player_id, role, game_date, tournament_id. Use TanStack Query caching. Lazy load chart libraries. Optimize component re-renders with React.memo if needed.

Maintain minimum 80% test coverage for all new code. Unit tests: Vitest for service logic and calculations. Component tests: React Testing Library for component rendering and interactions. Integration tests: Test API endpoints with various query parameters and error cases. E2E tests: Playwright for complete user flows. Test locations: tests/unit/services/, tests/components/analytics/, tests/integration/api/analytics/, tests/e2e/analytics/.

Handle API errors (network, 404, 400) with user-friendly messages via toast notifications or error boundaries. Display empty states for no data with helpful messaging. Handle missing scenario data gracefully with conditional rendering. Handle missing aggregated data gracefully (show win rates without comparison). Add retry logic for failed API calls (exponential backoff, 3 attempts). Use ErrorBoundary component for component errors.

Mobile-first approach with breakpoints: 320px, 768px, 1024px. Charts should be responsive (mobile: stacked, desktop: side-by-side). Use ResponsiveContainer from Recharts. Touch-optimized interactions (44x44px minimum touch targets). Responsive navigation patterns (mobile: bottom nav or hamburger menu, desktop: sidebar or top tabs).

interface.name: GET /api/players/[id]/analytics/win-rates
interface.description: API endpoint for win rate analysis. Accepts optional query parameters: dateRange (object with startDate, endDate, or preset), roles (array of PlayerRole). Returns WinRateAnalysisResponse. Requires authentication. Returns 404 if player not found, 400 for invalid parameters.

interface.name: WinRateAnalysis
interface.signature: interface WinRateAnalysis { overall: number; byRole: Record<string, number>; byScenario?: Record<string, number>; comparisonToAverage?: number; }
interface.description: Data model for win rate analysis. overall: overall win rate percentage (0-100). byRole: win rate percentage per role (DON, MAFIA, SHERIFF, CITIZEN). byScenario: optional win rate by scenario (tournament vs casual). comparisonToAverage: optional difference from average win rate.

interface.name: WinRateAnalysisResponse
interface.description: API response type for win rate analysis endpoint. Extends WinRateAnalysis interface.

interface.name: WinRateAnalysisProps
interface.signature: interface WinRateAnalysisProps { playerId: string; dateRange?: DateRange; roles?: PlayerRole[]; }
interface.description: Props for WinRateAnalysis component. playerId: UUID of player. dateRange: optional date range filter. roles: optional array of roles to filter by.

interface.name: WinRateAnalyzer
interface.signature: class WinRateAnalyzer { calculateOverallWinRate(data: GameParticipationData[]): number; calculatePerRoleWinRates(data: GameParticipationData[]): Record<string, number>; calculateScenarioWinRates(data: GameParticipationData[]): Record<string, number> | undefined; calculateComparisonToAverage(winRates: WinRateAnalysis, averageWinRates?: WinRateAnalysis): number | undefined; }
interface.description: Domain service for win rate calculations. Handles business logic for calculating overall win rate, per-role win rates, scenario-based win rates, and comparison to averages. Pure functions with no side effects.

interface.name: WinRateRepository
interface.signature: class WinRateRepository { getWinRateData(playerId: string, dateRange?: DateRange, roles?: PlayerRole[]): Promise<GameParticipationData[]>; verifyPlayerAccess(playerId: string, userId?: string): Promise<boolean>; }
interface.description: Repository for querying win rate data from database. Handles all database queries related to win rate analysis. Follows Repository pattern from Clean Architecture. Reference RoleMetricsRepository for implementation patterns.

interface.name: useWinRateAnalysis
interface.signature: function useWinRateAnalysis(playerId: string, dateRange?: DateRange, roles?: PlayerRole[]): { data: WinRateAnalysisResponse | undefined; isLoading: boolean; error: Error | null; }
interface.description: TanStack Query hook for fetching win rate data. Returns data, loading state, and error. Handles caching, refetching, and error states. Follows same pattern as useELOTrends hook.

interface.name: WinRateAnalysis component
interface.signature: function WinRateAnalysis({ playerId, dateRange, roles }: WinRateAnalysisProps): JSX.Element
interface.description: Main component for win rate analysis. Displays overall win rate, per-role breakdown, charts (bar chart and pie chart), scenario-based win rates (if available), comparison to averages (if available). Connects to analyticsStore for filters. Handles loading, error, and empty states.

interface.name: WinRateBarChart component
interface.signature: function WinRateBarChart({ data, roles }: { data: Record<string, number>; roles: PlayerRole[]; }): JSX.Element
interface.description: Bar chart component for comparing win rates across roles. Uses Recharts BarChart. Shows hover tooltips with exact percentages. Color-coded by role. Responsive with ResponsiveContainer. Smooth animations (300ms).

interface.name: WinLossPieChart component
interface.signature: function WinLossPieChart({ wins, losses }: { wins: number; losses: number; }): JSX.Element
interface.description: Pie chart component for win/loss distribution. Uses Recharts PieChart. Shows win/loss percentages. Color-coded (green for wins, red for losses). Responsive with ResponsiveContainer. Smooth animations (300ms).

tests.standards: Testing follows established patterns from previous analytics stories. Unit tests use Vitest for service logic and calculations with 80%+ coverage target. Component tests use React Testing Library for rendering, interactions, loading states, empty states, and chart rendering. Integration tests verify API endpoints with various query parameters, error cases, authentication, and database queries. E2E tests use Playwright for complete user flows including filter application and chart updates. Test locations: tests/unit/services/ for domain services, tests/components/analytics/ for components, tests/integration/api/analytics/ for API endpoints, tests/e2e/analytics/ for E2E tests. Performance testing verifies API response time < 500ms and chart rendering < 2 seconds.
